hero.title: Harshavardhana: The Last Great Emperor
hero.description: Harshavardhana's reign (606–647 CE) represents the transition between ancient and medieval India, marked by literary patronage and ambitious military expansion.

cards.details: Harsha ascends the throne of Thanesar after the death of his brother, Rajyavardhana.
Harsha finally consolidates his power and occupies the throne of Kannauj, shifting his capital.
The visit of Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang, providing a detailed record of Harsha's administration.
Death of Harsha; marks the end of the Pushyabhuti dynasty and the beginning of political fragmentation.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking Harsha as the founder of the Vardhana dynasty (It was Pushyabhuti).
Assuming Harsha controlled the entire Deccan (He was stopped by Pulakeshin II at the Narmada).
Believing Harsha was a devout Buddhist from birth (He was initially a Shaivite).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Capital: Thanesar (initial) to Kannauj (strategic center).
  • Influence: Controlled North India; Narmada was the southern boundary.

Personalities

  • Hiuen Tsang: Official chronicler of Harsha's court.
  • Banabhatta: Author of Harshacharita.
  • Pulakeshin II: Chalukya rival who checked Harsha's expansion.

Political Mindmap

  • Expansionism:
    • Defeat of Sasanka of Bengal.
    • Alliance with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa.
  • Administration:
    • Feudal system (Samantas).
    • Land grants and judicial system described by Hiuen Tsang.
  • Religious Policy:
    • Shaivism -> Mahayana Buddhism.
    • Kannauj Assembly (Buddhist debate).
    • Prayag Assembly (Grand charity/Mahamoksha Parishad).
